name: How to Compare Room Addition Cost per Square Foot in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How can I realistically compare per-square-foot prices for room additions across different Los Angeles County contractors?
mainEntity.text: How can I realistically compare per-square-foot prices for room additions across different Los Angeles County contractors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Per-square-foot pricing for room additions in Los Angeles County is often misleading because contractors include different items and quality levels. To make a fair comparison, start by providing all bidders with the same set of plans or at least the same written scope, including square footage, ceiling heights, and desired finishes. Ask each contractor to break down their estimate into major categories: foundation, framing, roofing, windows, insulation, drywall, finishes, fixtures, permits, design/engineering, and contingency. Request specific allowances for items like cabinetry, flooring, tile, and plumbing fixtures (e.g., dollar amount per square foot or per fixture) so you can see whether one bid assumes far cheaper products. Clarify whether structural upgrades to the existing home, utility upgrades, demolition, and debris hauling are included. Ask contractors to note any items they intentionally excluded, such as landscaping repair, fencing, or painting beyond the new area. Once you have itemized bids, calculate a “normalized” per-square-foot cost by removing clearly optional or unique items and aligning allowance levels. This will reveal which contractors are truly more economical and which are simply assuming lower quality or fewer required upgrades. Use these normalized numbers plus each contractor’s experience and communication style to make your decision, not just the headline cost.
acceptedAnswer.description: To compare room addition per-square-foot prices in Los Angeles County, standardize what is included: foundation, finishes, fixtures, structural upgrades, permits, and design. Request detailed, itemized bids, align allowance quality levels, and exclude clearly optional items so you evaluate similar scopes instead of headline numbers only.
